question: Dion is a whole man; Theon is Dion minus one foot. Dion's foot is cut off. Which survives, according to Chrysippus?
options: Both survive, now in one body
answer: Dion survives; Theon has perished. Philo reports the reasoning: two individuals cannot fill one and the same body, so one must go. Dion can survive losing a foot, as anyone can; Theon, though he lost nothing, is squeezed out. Many modern metaphysicians prefer the answer Chrysippus ruled out: two things sharing one body.
move: Surviving a loss and surviving a merger are different questions.
trap: Theon lost nothing, so surely it is Theon who survives.
reference: Sedley, The Stoic Criterion of Identity, Phronesis 27 (3), 1982
